R957.summary: Gottfried van Swieten at Bonn to Count Cobenzl at Brussels: the new convention leaves the revenues to France while reserving sovereignty to the Empress; the French act on it without any order from the court, causing much ill feeling; on France's behalf the Prince de Croÿ, who has claims to it, has been put in possession of the principality of Moers without the Empress, its sovereign, being told.
R957.en:

Empress. The French go on acting on that assumption, although we have no order from the court on the matter; this
causes a great deal of ill feeling. On France's behalf the Prince de Croÿ, who has claims to it, has just been put in
possession of the principality of Moers, without so much as informing the Empress, who is its sovereign.

R956.summary: On Soubise's army: no magazines are being made except at the expense of the exhausted Estates of the Empire, the principle being to keep the King's army without its costing a sou; the contributions of Guelders paid for his army and money was sent to Contades' army for winter quarters.
R956.en:
It is certain that the Prince de Soubise's army is in the best state imaginable … before the countryside is stocked,
«no one is thinking of making magazines» except «at the expense of the Estates of the Empire, which» are entirely
exhausted; the great principle seems to be to make «the King's army subsist there without its costing a sou». The past
campaign is proof of it; and so «the prince [147 100 126 148]» admitted that the «contributions of Guelders» had «sufficed
for the upkeep of his army» and that enough money had even been «sent to Contades's army» to meet the costs «of the
troops' pay during the winter», and that all the operations of the past year had «had no other aim. The prince thinks»
well, but the rest are «ill-intentioned»; besides that, «there is not one capable general officer in this army except
